elements.evidence: Section 13 as rendered still binds both parties ("Neither party shall ... solicit for hire ... any of the other party's personnel"), so Company/Customer remains subject to a non-solicit. The proposal narrows rather than deletes the covenant, so the preferred position is not reached.
Rendered clause opens "Neither party shall, ... solicit for hire ... any of the other party's personnel" — the obligation runs in both directions and was untouched by the edit.

elements.element: The restriction covers only personnel directly involved in the Services.
elements.evidence: Retained scope language: "any of the other party's personnel who have had direct involvement with the Services" — limited to Services-involved personnel, not all personnel.

elements.element: The restriction lasts no longer than 12 months after the person's involvement ends.
elements.evidence: Operation 1 replaced "during the term of this Agreement and for one (1) year after its termination" with "for twelve (12) months after the end of the relevant individual's involvement with the Services" — the temporal anchor is now the end of the individual's involvement and the duration is exactly twelve months.

elements.element: General advertisements are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Added sentence: "The foregoing restriction does not apply to general advertisements or other solicitations not specifically directed at the other party's personnel".

elements.element: Unsolicited approaches are excluded from the restriction.
elements.evidence: Same added sentence continues: "or to responses to unsolicited approaches by such personnel".

elements.element: The restriction does not prohibit hiring.
elements.evidence: The operative prohibition is on soliciting ("solicit for hire as an employee, consultant or otherwise"); no no-hire or "shall not employ or engage" language appears in the rendered clause, and none was added.

reasons: Fallback checklist is complete on the operative language: mutuality and Services-involvement scope were already present, the two edits supply the 12-month involvement-anchored duration and both carve-outs, and the clause remains solicitation-only with no no-hire.
Preferred is not met and the finding does not claim it — the covenant survives against Customer in narrowed form; correctly classified as a deviation redlined to fallback.

Minimality holds: only the duration phrase was replaced (it had to be, since "during the term ... and for one (1) year after its termination" is the exact defect) and a single carve-out sentence was inserted. No survival tail, expense language, damages, procedure or boilerplate extras; the consent mechanic ("without such other party's express written consent, which shall not be unreasonably withheld") and the rest of the clause were left intact.

Intent preserved: no defined term is orphaned, "Services" remains the defined term used elsewhere, and no retained sentence contradicts the new twelve-month anchor or the carve-outs. The deleted term-plus-one-year language is not favourable retained language — it is the non-conforming duration the checklist requires be fixed.

Deterministic evidence checks out in substance, not just mechanically: the duration regex maps to an actual involvement-end anchor rather than a termination-date anchor, and the carve-out check corresponds to a real sentence covering both general advertisements and unsolicited approaches.
